notes: v743 - the lessons are corrected where testing proved them wrong, and a new lesson 55 teaches how a backtest flatters itself. Lessons 11 and 38 described the Hunter preset as winning about half its trades. That figure came from a run whose signal scores were computed across the whole graded period, so picks were filtered using information from their own future. Re-tested window by window, using only what was knowable on each day, it wins about a THIRD of its trades. Both lessons now say so and point at the correction. New lesson 55 covers the five faults found in our own testing: look-ahead in the scores; a single random run being treated as a benchmark when it needs to be a distribution; slippage ladders whose rungs are not the same book, because changing costs changes which shares get bought; concentration measured in summed percentages instead of dollars; and survivorship - no company that delisted in the last ten years is in the stored history, so every long-window figure is an upper bound. It also covers the cost line: an edge below the round-trip brokerage is not a small winner, it is a loser. What survived all five corrections is stated plainly - the trailing exit still beats a fixed take-profit, the sub-$1 band still beats the rest, and graded evidence still beats properly-run random picks. The direction held every time; the size was optimistic every time. Nothing in the app's behaviour changed, only what it teaches. Practice money only. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5).
